_README: Decision briefs — the single source of truth for OPEN decisions needing Bilal. The roadmap's Decision queue table is the index; this file carries the evidence, options, and recommendation, and the dashboard renders it as answerable cards. When a decision is answered (GitHub issue or in person): set status='decided', fill 'decided', and reflect the outcome into VERSED_TRANSLATION_ROADMAP.md in the same commit. Agents: read this file to know what is blocked and why; never invent an answer for an open decision.

decisions.title: Genre coverage: how do we stop the benchmark being 99.6% hadith?
decisions.blocks: Every measured number in the project. Nothing generalizes past hadith until this is answered, and the benchmark cannot be frozen.
decisions.question: The draft benchmark is 1,107 hadith items out of 1,111. Where does genre diversity actually come from?
decisions.why_now: This gates the benchmark rebuild, and the rebuild gates re-running the bakeoff and QE study. Deciding it late means paying for those runs twice. D1d is now resolved, so ATHAR is usable — but it still has no per-row genre metadata, so it cannot supply the genre axis by itself.
evidence: 1,107 of 1,111 draft_test items are LK Hadith; ATHAR contributes 4. Zero tafsir, philosophy, adab, history, poetry.

ATHAR's parquet files carry ONLY (arabic, english) columns — no per-row work, author, or genre metadata exists. Verified against both train and test schemas (src/versed_translator/benchmark/assemble.py:20).
ATHAR's median item is 18 Arabic words, below the benchmark's own 30-word band floor — that, not a sampling bug, is why only 4 rows survived.
Hadith is unusually formulaic (isnad chains, fixed openings). A model that handles it well may fail on Sufi metaphor or legal reasoning and we would not see it.

corpus/PD_TRANSLATIONS.md (compiled 2026-08-12) lists 16 PD translations across 9 genres with verified archive.org URLs — the genres the benchmark is missing are all covered. PD rationales are translator-death-year/pre-1930 heuristics, not cleared legal opinions (D6b still gates commercial use), and their archaic register is D1a's question.

options.label: Targeted passage alignment from the 16 PD translations (benchmark-scale only)
options.detail: Bilal's question surfaced this and it beats a/b/c. corpus/PD_TRANSLATIONS.md already inventories 16 public-domain English translations across 9 genres, every one with a verified archive.org URL — history, biography, philosophy, adab/maqama, fables, poetry, travel, sira, scripture. The blocker was never FINDING translations; it is aligning them. But a benchmark needs a few hundred passages, not whole books: hand-aligning (or LLM-proposes/human-checks) ~40 passages each from 5-8 works is a fraction of building the general C7 engine, and yields exactly the genre spread the benchmark lacks. Best starting works: Baladhuri/Hitti, Ibn Khallikan/de Slane (each biography is a natural alignment unit), Hariri/Chenery.

options.label: Email the ATHAR author for per-work/genre provenance
options.detail: Combine with the D1d license question — one email, two possible unlocks. Costs nothing and may hand us the genre axis outright. Does not block starting (b) in parallel.

options.label: Add a sub-30-word band so ATHAR's diversity counts
options.detail: Cheap interim fix. Gets ATHAR's sentence-level material into the benchmark immediately, but genre labels stay coarse until (a) answers.

options.label: Accept hadith-only for v0.1; get genre via PD alignment in v0.2
options.detail: Honest and already labeled that way. But it pulls C7 (Versed Align) forward, which is a genuinely bigger scope — take it deliberately, never by drift.

decisions.recommendation: Take (d): targeted passage alignment from the PD list, benchmark-scale only. It gets real genre coverage without waiting for C7, and without the ATHAR metadata that does not exist. (b) remains a cheap parallel add. (a) is now moot for licensing — D1d resolved without it — though the author could still confirm whether per-work provenance exists.

decided.note: DECIDED: targeted passage alignment from the 16 PD translations, benchmark-scale only. Genre coverage comes from public-domain English translations (history, biography, philosophy, adab/maqama, fables, poetry, travel, sira, scripture) rather than from ATHAR, which has no per-row genre metadata and sits below the 30-word band floor. Explicitly NOT waiting for C7: a benchmark needs a few hundred aligned passages, not whole aligned books. ATHAR email is NO LONGER NEEDED for this decision or for D1d (resolved independently). The only residual value in contacting the author is per-work provenance for C8 training-corpus stratification — revisit at C8, not now.

decisions.title: Make structured block translation with ID preservation the production contract?
decisions.blocks: The C5 router design, and the worst known safety gap in the whole system.
decisions.question: Should production always translate in ID-preserving structured blocks, so a dropped block is directly observable?
decisions.why_now: It is a one-line architectural decision that dissolves a failure mode no detector we have can catch. Deciding it before the router is built avoids designing detection for a problem we can define away.
evidence: Partial clause removal is undetectable from (source, output) alone on unpunctuated classical Arabic: sentence_ratio_flag cannot run and a truncated output stays inside the normal Arabic→English expansion band.
COMETKiwi also misses it — 22.9% detection, and a NEGATIVE mean delta, meaning it scores truncated text HIGHER than the complete translation.
So neither the neural signal nor the deterministic checks cover the single highest-severity omission failure. It is asserted as a known gap in tests/test_checks.py so it cannot regress silently.
The harness already supports the structured template — this costs implementation discipline, not new code.

NEW 2026-08-14: this would solve a SECOND independent problem. 39% of MetricX-QE inputs blow past its 1536-token window, which roughly doubles the apparent error score and corrupts the QE matrix for long passages. Short ID-tagged blocks stay inside the window. Two separate measured failures, one fix.

options.label: Yes — structured blocks with IDs are the production contract
options.detail: A dropped or truncated block becomes structurally visible instead of semantically invisible. Cheaper than any detection scheme we could build.

options.label: No — keep free-form translation, invest in detection
options.detail: Means accepting that the highest-severity omission failure stays undetectable, or funding an LLM verifier pass to catch it.

decisions.recommendation: Yes. It converts a detection problem we have measurably failed to solve into a structural property we get for free.

decisions.title: How should QE handle passages longer than the model's token window?
decisions.blocks: Trusting the QE matrix on long passages — which is exactly where silent omission, the failure we care most about, actually happens.
decisions.question: 39% of MetricX-QE inputs exceed its 1536-token window. Do we chunk, translate in blocks, exclude those rows, or change model?
decisions.why_now: It biases results in the study now running, and it is the second problem that D2e (structured blocks) would solve — so the two decisions should be made together, not separately.
evidence: 126 of 324 smoke inputs (39%) hit the 1536-token cap.
Truncation roughly doubles the apparent error score: median 17.51 for truncated inputs vs 8.88 for inputs that fit.
Truncation eats the END of 'source: ... candidate: ...' — that is, the candidate being judged, not the source.

Length-increasing corruptions get truncated more than their clean counterparts, biasing their deltas toward zero. The duplicate_sentence result (5% detection, negative mean delta) is an artifact of this cap, NOT a property of MetricX.
This hits the 250-600 word band hardest — the long passages where silent omission is most likely and most consequential.
Instrumented but deliberately not fixed: the scorer counts truncations and the runner stamps truncated_inputs/truncated_fraction into the summary, so no result can silently hide it.

options.label: Adopt structured block translation (same as D2e) and let blocks be the QE unit
options.detail: Blocks stay well inside the window, so truncation mostly disappears. Solves this AND the clause-removal gap with one architectural choice. Decide it together with D2e.

options.label: Chunk long passages and aggregate the scores
options.detail: Works without changing the translation contract, but aggregation across chunks is its own calibration problem and QE scores do not average cleanly.

options.label: Exclude truncated rows from the matrix and report the coverage loss
options.detail: Honest and cheap, but it blinds QE precisely on the longest passages — the ones where omission matters most.

options.label: Use a longer-context QE model
options.detail: MetricX-24 XL/XXL share the same 1536 window, so this likely means leaving the MetricX family — and its Apache-2.0 licence is the reason it is a candidate at all.

decisions.recommendation: Take the blocks option, together with D2e. One architectural decision retires two separately-measured failures; the alternatives each buy back only one and add calibration work.

decisions.title: Provision the remaining provider API keys, or formally descope the bakeoff field?
decisions.blocks: Closing out C2 and ratifying D2a. Currently carried as ambient blockage, which is the worst of both.
decisions.question: Do we get Gemini / Qwen-MT / DeepSeek keys, or do we record the bakeoff field as deliberately narrowed?
decisions.why_now: Every session so far has listed 'no API keys' as a gap without either fixing it or dropping it. Either answer unblocks; carrying it does not.
evidence: TG27B (open, Modal H100) and Claude Sonnet 5 tied on hadith: chrF 50.24 vs 50.60, both 139/139 clean.
TG27B ran ~36x faster (0.68s vs 24.5s mean) at ~$0.27 for the whole set.
C8 requires an OPEN, fine-tunable base. Gemini / DeepSeek-API / Qwen-MT-API cannot be that regardless of their scores, so they do not actually compete for the production-translator slot.
The missing legs answer a different question — what a pure-API corpus route would cost — which only matters if fine-tuning fails at D8a.

options.label: Descope the field to TG27B / TG12B / Claude ceiling
options.detail: Record D2a as decided-by-field. Revisit the API route only if D8a (fine-tune GO/NO-GO) fails. Fastest path to a closed C2.

options.label: Provision the keys this week and run the full field
options.detail: Gives a complete comparison table and a real API-route cost baseline. Costs money and a session, and does not change the likely D2a outcome.

decisions.recommendation: Descope, with the TG12B Modal leg still run — the 12B-vs-27B gap is the number that actually drives serving economics and has never been measured.

decided.note: Bilal provided DeepSeek and Qwen/DashScope keys (stored in gitignored .env, mode 600; repo is public so they must never be committed). Gemini key NOT provided — the Gemini leg stays descoped unless a key arrives. D2a is therefore NOT decided-by-field: DeepSeek and Qwen-MT can now run. Sequencing unchanged: do NOT run these legs on the hadith-only benchmark with the mismatched Modal prompt — fold them into the single post-D1e measurement suite with matched prompts, per the no-re-measurement-treadmill rule.

decisions.title: ATHAR license conflict — which license is actually intended?
decisions.blocks: Using ATHAR in the C8 training corpus. Currently held at eval-internal.
decisions.question: ATHAR's dataset card says CC-BY-SA-4.0 in its YAML and CC-BY-NC-4.0 in its prose. Which governs?
decisions.why_now: The same email should carry the D1e metadata question. One message, two unlocks — and the answer takes days to come back, so it should be out now.
evidence: ATHAR is the largest source we have: 66,043 pairs (65,043 train + 1,000 native test).
Card YAML says CC-BY-SA-4.0; card prose says CC-BY-NC-4.0. NC would bar it from anything Versed ships commercially.
Held at rights_status=eval_internal until resolved, so it is currently unusable for C8 training data.

options.label: Email the author now, combined with the D1e metadata question
options.detail: One message: which license is intended, and does per-work/genre provenance exist for the pairs?

options.label: Assume NC and keep it eval-internal permanently
options.detail: Safe but costs us the largest parallel source for training, and we never find out whether that was necessary.

decisions.recommendation: Send the combined email. Assume NC in the meantime so nothing blocks on the reply.

decided.note: Bilal researched the provenance and resolved it without needing the author email. Kandil7/Athar-Datasets (created April 2026) carries HF structured license `mit` AND README prose explicitly permitting commercial use — no conflict there. The 'research and personal use' prose survives only in the later Shamela4 repos (AuthenticIlm/Shamela4_Full_DB, extracted 2026-04-26; Kandil7/Athar-Shamela4, duplicated 2026-06-02), which ALSO carry `license: mit` in structured metadata. Reading: stale prose retained while repo-level license was set to MIT, not a deliberate non-commercial designation. No commit explicitly documenting a license change was found, so this is a well-supported inference, not documentary proof. CONCLUSION: treat the ATHAR dataset/extraction as MIT / commercially usable. IMPORTANT CARVE-OUT: MIT cannot grant copyright the dataset creator does not own. Modern third-party matter inside source works — editor introductions (مقدمة المحقق), modern commentary — must be filtered. Ancient source text is the part we rely on. The Shamela4 `is_hidden: true` flag marks books with copyright/access restrictions and is consistent with this reading.

decisions.title: Approve and send the OpenITI letter
decisions.blocks: Nothing immediately — but the answer takes weeks and gates commercial use, so lead time is the whole point.
decisions.question: Is the drafted OpenITI letter approved to send?
decisions.why_now: Drafted 2026-08-12 and still unsent. It is pure lead time: the reply arrives while we build, or it does not arrive and we learn that too.
evidence: Draft ready at OPENITI_LETTER_DRAFT.md (gitignored, local-only).

Asks: we strip OpenITI markup/metadata and use only the underlying public-domain Arabic strings, most originating in pre-existing digital libraries; we create our own segmentation, translations, and audio. Is BY-NC-SA intended to cover those underlying strings or OpenITI's annotations and corpus-database? Would you grant Versed commercial permission for this public-access project?
Nothing in the roadmap blocks on the answer except commercial exploitation (D6b counsel is the other half).

options.label: Approve and send as drafted
options.detail: Starts the clock. The reply informs D6b (counsel) and the C12 release licensing.

options.label: Revise first — I want to change the framing
options.detail: Say what to change and it gets redrafted before sending.

decisions.recommendation: Send as drafted. It is lead time we cannot buy back later.
